title: Matriarchal Glue Is Only So Sticky

contact_edits.before: Derek Boyes seems whimsically out of place as her perennially defeated husband, substituting a Celtic smile for a Yiddish shrug. William Webster might profitably be more whimsical as Jacob, who retreats by playing Caruso records, but he does the secular-prophet bit imposingly well. A shame that he has to make his greatest contribution to the plot from offstage. Michael Hanrahan, with a silk scarf wrapped around his vocal chords, is absolutely right as the familys comparatively rich Uncle Morty, and Ari Cohen righter than right as Moe whose amputation on the last day of the war made him a cynic, a pacifist and--as it transpires -- an unlikely do-gooder. The young people are very impressive: Jonathan Gould quivering with life as the irresolute Ralph, Sarah Wilson hard as nails as Hennie and Matthew Edison is lovely as the poor schmuck tricked into giving Hennie's child a father. It would be hard, and probably wrong, to play the last life-affirming moments for irony. But taken straight they seem wished for, tacked-on. Play and production are awake, no question, but they don't sing. - Awake and Sing! runs through July 31 at the Young Centre for the Performing Arts. Visit youngcentre.cafor details. robert.cushman@hotmail.com
